title: Riskified’s holiday guide is here
summary: The message for merchants? Don’t let your guard down when volume is low, because fraudsters don’t take a holiday.
body_markdown:
**And we’re seeing a risk pattern you can’t ignore** .


It’s Christmas Eve, the gifting rush is over. In categories like electronics and fast fashion, sales drop by half in the days right before the holiday as shipping cutoffs pass, and shoppers pivot to items like gift cards for last-minute purchases. Time for fraud teams to take a breath, right?


Here’s the thing: those lower-volume days during the holidays can actually be the riskiest when it comes to fraud. Here’s why.


## **When volume falls, risk rises**


[Riskified data](https://www.riskified.com/resources/guide/holiday-ecommerce-fraud-and-abuse-management/) shows again and again that while the total volume of fraud grows along with legitimate sales at the holidays, the proportion of fraudulent order attempts actually peaks when volume is lowest.


For example, in both 2024 and 2025, Christmas Eve orders for electronics dropped by about half in the US, but it was the riskiest day of the entire year for fraud **.** That pattern was nearly identical for fast fashion.


While peak sales days vary by product and region around the world, this risk pattern is surprisingly universal: the busiest days aren’t the riskiest.


The message for merchants? Don’t let your guard down when volume is low, because fraudsters don’t take a holiday. In fact, there’s dark web evidence indicating they actually anticipate and exploit a reduction in merchant vigilance during the holiday chaos.


We don’t recommend cancelling all December PTO. But when attacks land as teams step away, retailers need automatic detection and fast response mechanisms in place to protect their holiday revenue.


You’ll find timely recommendations in Riskified’s 2026[holiday guide](https://www.riskified.com/resources/guide/holiday-ecommerce-fraud-and-abuse-management/) : **The gift of secure ecommerce, for every order and every customer** . It draws on exclusive merchant-network data, shopper research and dark web intelligence to uncover the trends shaping the season ahead. From past years’ Black Friday Cyber Monday (BFCM) through January’s surge in returns and disputes, it will help you secure seasonal opportunities and manage risk across the peaks and valleys.


In addition to the predictable patterns merchants can’t ignore, the guide offers a look at some newer vectors that will impact risk and revenue this year, including:


- **Risks across the journey.** The holidays will bring new risks from account setup all the way to returns and dispute resolution in January.
- **More delegated commerce (beyond checkout).** About 68% of consumers plan to use AI for holiday shopping this year, and AI is changing how consumers discover products, make purchases and manage post-purchase requests.
- **Risk trends by category and region.** Learn how new customers factor into the holiday risk equation and other trends across gift cards, electronics, high-end goods, fast fashion, and sneakers in the US, EU, APAC and Mexico.
- **Risk outliers.** Riskified analysts looked at the exceptions, too. Fast fashion in APAC bucks the trend when it comes to the risk vs volume correlation. And for sneakers, it’s a whole different ballgame. Risk levels are less elastic, existing customers can be just as risky as newcomers, and release days play by their own rules entirely.


[The guide](https://www.riskified.com/resources/guide/holiday-ecommerce-fraud-and-abuse-management/) translates these findings into six practical strategies for the season, data and recommendations your team needs to navigate peak season, capture more legitimate sales and protect customer trust from the first click through the final refund or dispute.
